<!-- evidence:f4281ec5ddc49818f1d093a7 source:Vendor Instructions!A1 -->
                                       VENDOR SECURITY QUESTIONNAIRE INSTRUCTIONS

<!-- evidence:6722a3217dd03d85fd5bcf1b source:Vendor Instructions!A6 -->
Thank you for your interest in working with us!
We appreciate your time and effort in completing our vendor questionnaire. This step is an important part of our evaluation process to ensure that all vendors meet our standards for quality, security, and compliance. Your responses will help us determine if we can move forward together. Please provide accurate and complete information, as this will allow us to review your application more promptly. 

Please pay close attention to any informational hints and instructions included throughout the questionnaire. These notes are designed to guide you and ensure your responses meet our requirements. Taking a moment to review them carefully will help avoid delays in the approval process.

Once you’ve completed the workbook and gathered any requested documentation or evidence, please email everything back to the contact who originally sent you the questionnaire. If you have any questions or concerns at any point, feel free to reach out to us at your Regodit contact—we’re happy to assist.

<!-- evidence:bb90d087e4808c41554ea2ee source:Vendor Instructions!A22 -->
Step 1: Complete the Vendor Profile tab. 

<!-- evidence:91f55d0f0cf603cf18fd776f source:Vendor Instructions!A23 -->
Complete the Vendor Profile tab fully and the last row will tell you if you need to fill out the Vendor Security Responses tab and/or what to do next.

<!-- evidence:d2b27ef60f43401dc69b6ed4 source:Vendor Instructions!A24 -->
Step 2: Follow the “Next Steps” field.

<!-- evidence:f79547f4370fbf1daa7a0652 source:Vendor Instructions!A25 -->
The next steps field will indicate whether to email us the completed Vendor Profile or continue to the Vendor Security Responses tab.

<!-- evidence:efb953597854b2995a55642a source:Vendor Instructions!A26 -->
Step 3: Package and send everything.

<!-- evidence:bd77b1db7d8057ba70ec2d0f source:Vendor Instructions!A27 -->
Email the entire workbook and any requested supporting documents to your Client XYZ contact

<!-- evidence:205266cf68d3b0204bdf1d0b source:Definitions!A1 -->
Vendor Criticality (SC)

<!-- evidence:d6f9fe91b70e717cb763d2ad source:Definitions!B1 -->
Definition

<!-- evidence:41044a9086fc360c9d58bc33 source:Definitions!C1 -->
Example Scenario

<!-- evidence:c80701832f37def84569cd14 source:Definitions!F1 -->
 Tab Name

<!-- evidence:9cb3f19c81e1719ebd89d021 source:Definitions!G1 -->
Quick Link

<!-- evidence:1cba31f8379e0c183c18e95e source:Definitions!A2 -->
SC1: Mission Critical

<!-- evidence:24631dcfab87ee35be6af65e source:Definitions!B2 -->
Vendor failure would cause immediate or near‑immediate company‑wide business stoppage, major revenue loss, severe reputational harm, regulatory exposure, or risk to health/safety. Operations cannot tolerate more than 24 hours of disruption.

<!-- evidence:f8c5aa84ccfdc2e5311e7116 source:Definitions!C2 -->
Cloud provider hosting your main customer portal; vendor managing payment processing for all clients.

<!-- evidence:fd7e480bbd10c8c6cf7575c1 source:Definitions!F2 -->
 Vendor Instructions

<!-- evidence:9cabd0705a3bd0f88d22e05f source:Definitions!G2 -->
Formula: =HYPERLINK("#'Vendor Instructions'!A1","Go to Vendor Instructions"); source cached value: 'Go to Vendor Instructions' (not independently recalculated)

<!-- evidence:978bb44581aead2d1d843f1b source:Definitions!A3 -->
SC2: Business Critical

<!-- evidence:db0bf490ee52d886f3105492 source:Definitions!B3 -->
Vendor failure would cause major delays or stoppages lasting more than 24 hours but no more than 5 business days in important business functions, with measurable operational or short‑term customer impact.

<!-- evidence:5a347eeb696c4bd8b654c05c source:Definitions!C3 -->
Payroll processor; vendor managing company email; facilities vendor controlling building access.

<!-- evidence:fca912bf85e7b15b1ad4eb98 source:Definitions!F3 -->
 Vendor Profile

<!-- evidence:dce29e21a49d517a45e06ce2 source:Definitions!G3 -->
Formula: =HYPERLINK("#'Vendor Profile'!A1","Go to Vendor Profile"); source cached value: 'Go to Vendor Profile' (not independently recalculated)

<!-- evidence:0881867f439631ba803f914b source:Definitions!A4 -->
SC3: Non-Critical

<!-- evidence:7e7380af0b7f78d78306bf3a source:Definitions!B4 -->
Vendor failure would cause inconvenience or extended delays (>5 business days up to 30 days), but would not stop core business operations. Impact is primarily on internal productivity, reporting, or indirect revenue, and is tolerable for several weeks.

<!-- evidence:49a670242381ecc109d37e5a source:Definitions!C4 -->
Vendor providing internal reporting tools; logistics partner for non-essential shipments.

<!-- evidence:6a8ff5abb239a5d0050a23d8 source:Definitions!F4 -->
 Vendor Security Responses

<!-- evidence:07f9e4cb47a3c8f292edb092 source:Definitions!G4 -->
Formula: =HYPERLINK("#'Vendor Security Responses'!A1","Go to Vendor Security Responses"); source cached value: 'Go to Vendor Security Responses' (not independently recalculated)

<!-- evidence:c9f5753eda11b1c573a1b5ea source:Definitions!A5 -->
SC4: Business Supporting

<!-- evidence:323d621381be1c9698a7e3e1 source:Definitions!B5 -->
Vendor failure would have minimal, localized, or easily absorbed impact, with no material effect on revenue, regulatory obligations, or customer satisfaction, even if unavailable for 30+ days.

<!-- evidence:92d4d0f61461afb4a44a9807 source:Definitions!C5 -->
Vendor supplying office supplies; team-level productivity tool; marketing swag provider.

<!-- evidence:dfcf22c0ce9e3f231b6a31f8 source:Definitions!A27 -->
Vendor Type

<!-- evidence:234bb371209b663a11cdd583 source:Definitions!B27 -->
Definition / Example

<!-- evidence:6cd7386fbc8f24a2cb71f202 source:Definitions!A28 -->
Technology Provider

<!-- evidence:7a4be0e2b9c7da15453d0e4d source:Definitions!B28 -->
Supplies technology solutions (hardware, software, IT infrastructure). E.g., Cisco, Dell, Microsoft.

<!-- evidence:bbbea3bd2b8a64c7ae17f9ef source:Definitions!A29 -->
Cloud Service Provider

<!-- evidence:d0518f462b9f7d5a390d70b0 source:Definitions!B29 -->
Delivers cloud-based services (storage, hosting, SaaS, IaaS, PaaS). E.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud.

<!-- evidence:598b2de42c3d5fc71c37388b source:Definitions!A30 -->
Managed Service Provider (MSP)

<!-- evidence:8f18e5b96446e47e854f9b96 source:Definitions!B30 -->
Manages IT services for your company (may include support, monitoring, maintenance). E.g., CDW, Rackspace.

<!-- evidence:fd13b44a6cd63f96ebb93828 source:Definitions!A31 -->
Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP)

<!-- evidence:61ccf69c691e540cdd32a76c source:Definitions!B31 -->
Specializes in security services like monitoring, threat detection, and incident response. E.g., Secureworks, Trustwave.

<!-- evidence:4f40227408d384584687b77c source:Definitions!A32 -->
Software Vendor

<!-- evidence:65cae0ab505d03176325414f source:Definitions!B32 -->
Develops or sells software applications. E.g., Adobe, Atlassian.

<!-- evidence:f43d8de3e336be4354d0a36d source:Definitions!A33 -->
Hardware Vendor

<!-- evidence:1008c0a0ee730ca1b627d2ce source:Definitions!B33 -->
Provides physical devices or equipment. E.g., Lenovo, HP.

<!-- evidence:f78e3ee89013ecc50b45b71a source:Definitions!A34 -->
Consulting/Professional Services

<!-- evidence:e5640308ad55105547887f0c source:Definitions!B34 -->
Offers expert advice or professional services. E.g., Deloitte, Accenture.

<!-- evidence:b087c07ec19ab64841d9f8f4 source:Definitions!A35 -->
Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)

<!-- evidence:8a57dd936d7202a7f7d4757d source:Definitions!B35 -->
Handles business processes (e.g., payroll, customer service) on your behalf. E.g., ADP, Concentrix.

<!-- evidence:d1ecf9769320cfdc5bc2ef05 source:Definitions!A36 -->
Facilities/Physical Security

<!-- evidence:be49f610a48c1fd221a9f73a source:Definitions!B36 -->
Manages physical security or facilities. E.g., security guard companies, building management.

<!-- evidence:bb31492ef2f5bf449ed3b6d0 source:Definitions!A37 -->
Logistics/Transportation

<!-- evidence:a15219cc4983157607ade6ac source:Definitions!B37 -->
Provides shipping, delivery, or transportation services. E.g., FedEx, UPS.

<!-- evidence:6fbca606d42b39c18b190a0d source:Definitions!A38 -->
Marketing/Advertising

<!-- evidence:d71675cfe0d2bc2e026b662d source:Definitions!B38 -->
Delivers marketing, advertising, or PR services. E.g., Ogilvy, Edelman.

<!-- evidence:eace669e4d99e66ca243cdad source:Definitions!A39 -->
Financial Services

<!-- evidence:f25021643b1b843403597e2f source:Definitions!B39 -->
Offers banking, payment processing, or financial consulting. E.g., Bank of America, PayPal.

<!-- evidence:c0d4759fd0292adbbd03a17c source:Definitions!A40 -->
Legal/Compliance

<!-- evidence:54097db1b2870fb75f15a507 source:Definitions!B40 -->
Provides legal advice or compliance services. E.g., law firms, compliance consultants.

<!-- evidence:f6a27b83773f450bc54093a9 source:Definitions!A41 -->
Other

<!-- evidence:4ada9911bcd961807288b2d6 source:Definitions!B41 -->
Any vendor not fitting the above categories.

<!-- evidence:d96bb69d329d0806145b1a4e source:Definitions!A43 -->
Security Questionnaire Assessment Result/Status

<!-- evidence:75b8d1242b57957b688f8f34 source:Definitions!B43 -->
Definition

<!-- evidence:fc6e4c40cdfa8d24bbaa3be3 source:Definitions!A44 -->
Approved

<!-- evidence:c4fe0b63f4c19586242514fc source:Definitions!B44 -->
The vendor or item has successfully met all requirements and has been formally accepted. No further action is needed.

<!-- evidence:82e7a785b52485d74e8849d7 source:Definitions!A45 -->
Rejected

<!-- evidence:f09377641d9c97c11828933a source:Definitions!B45 -->
The vendor or item did not meet the necessary requirements or standards and has been formally declined. The process is stopped for this vendor/item.

<!-- evidence:4d825b43def591b22d3eba48 source:Definitions!A46 -->
Review in Progress

<!-- evidence:34356e37ee59cf5e1a9e9e47 source:Definitions!B46 -->
The vendor or item is currently under evaluation. The review process is ongoing and a final decision has not yet been made.

<!-- evidence:05676dd06bab9ab0552c0e00 source:Definitions!A47 -->
Escalation in Progress

<!-- evidence:0234be9926cb0d1c4af6f19d source:Definitions!B47 -->
The review has encountered issues or risks that require higher-level review or approval. The case is being escalated to management or a specialized team for further scrutiny and approval.

<!-- evidence:dabfb56b77a77a02e4da778c source:Definitions!A49 -->
3rd Party Cert Assessment Result/Status

<!-- evidence:a52281d8ea19faed92e41b86 source:Definitions!B49 -->
Definition

<!-- evidence:d9b31ea18466124a097d4fdd source:Definitions!A50 -->
Approved

<!-- evidence:5f02c693b928069b9ba4a7d4 source:Definitions!B50 -->
The vendor or item has met all requirements and has been formally accepted. No further action is needed.

<!-- evidence:b4477560c5ee5f368a30b8c4 source:Definitions!A51 -->
Approved with Exception

<!-- evidence:8dd7cd6616448a0ef691a621 source:Definitions!B51 -->
The vendor or item is accepted, but one or more risks or requirements have been formally excepted (approved as an exception). An exception record is created and tracked.

<!-- evidence:a8f78e47c0354045352d7234 source:Definitions!A52 -->
Rejected

<!-- evidence:8939add8cdd8a123ed228930 source:Definitions!B52 -->
The vendor or item did not meet the necessary requirements or standards and has been formally declined. The process is stopped for this vendor/item.

<!-- evidence:9f3b1fabd1dc669aff9423ca source:Definitions!A53 -->
Escalated -  Pending Decision

<!-- evidence:a9bc2d6a946cdb18ce94398f source:Definitions!B53 -->
The review has been escalated to higher management or a specialized team for further review , and a final decision is still pending.

<!-- evidence:6af7190506efa59e2bb93c41 source:Definitions!A54 -->
Full Questionnaire Required

<!-- evidence:60519c2d8128bd36fc281b29 source:Definitions!B54 -->
The initial review is not sufficient; the vendor must complete the full security or risk questionnaire for further evaluation.

<!-- evidence:bc13a7cf0e6461e93db4ef84 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A2 -->
Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (CDPP)

<!-- evidence:1547ec9f63519d7e74e1bb54 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B2 -->
 Vendor shall implement and maintain a consolidated Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (“CDPP”) that documents the organization’s cybersecurity and data protection policies and standards in a single comprehensive policy, in the form attached hereto as Exhibit [X], which shall be reviewed and updated annually by Vendor. All material modifications to the CDPP shall be disclosed to Regodit immediately upon implementation. No modification may result in any objective degradation to the security of Regodit Data, the manner in which the Services are provided, or which fall below the standard of any applicable law. 

<!-- evidence:2f08fd5622bb1ab7f0d1ee86 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C2 -->
 

<!-- evidence:c328c599ca9f2dd3be5c7dfb source:Legal Clause Definitions!D2 -->
Regodit requires all  vendors maintain a comprehensive and unified Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program. A consolidated program provides clear governance, consistent application of security and privacy controls, and ensures all personnel are aware of and comply with organizational requirements. Regodit cannot accept the risk of outdated standards and gaps in coverage, which can lead to data breaches, regulatory non-compliance, and operational vulnerabilities. 

<!-- evidence:5892bfceeab3e400159c7f40 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E2 -->

<!-- evidence:cd6cab47db1ec7f5aab90f09 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A3 -->
Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (CDPP)

<!-- evidence:43b1326412b5609800a396e1 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B3 -->
[Vendor shall implement and maintain a Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (“CDPP”) that consolidates the organization’s cybersecurity and data protection policies and standards into a single documented policy.] The CDPP shall: (a) be disseminated to all relevant personnel to ensure awareness and compliance; (b) be reviewed and updated at least annually or as business or technology changes require to maintain compliance with statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements; (c) be enforced through standardized operating procedures integrated into daily business practices; and (d) extend through Vendor’s supply chain via contractual requirements for subcontractors and all other third parties that may directly or indirectly impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Regodit’s technology assets or Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:884e919551df126191bc9598 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C3 -->
 

<!-- evidence:9996bd981d5c6402266dbc23 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D3 -->
Regodit requires all vendors maintain a unified, executive-endorsed cybersecurity framework that is documented, regularly updated, and communicated to all relevant personnel. This approach provides complete coverage of data privacy controls, supports audit readiness, and prevents inconsistent practices that could expose Regodit to compliance and security vulnerabilities.

<!-- evidence:4c55c5d95cc0c9881ba6ca39 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E3 -->

<!-- evidence:e05ea653d1e633368b013803 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A4 -->
Cybersecurity Governance and Management

<!-- evidence:7f568fc7779e11cee612cb7a source:Legal Clause Definitions!B4 -->
 Vendor shall designate a qualified Security Officer with overall authority for managing the CDPP and performing or delegating the following responsibilities: (a) establish, document, and distribute cybersecurity and data protection policies, standards, and procedures to all applicable personnel and subcontractors; (b) monitor and analyze security alerts and information; (c) distribute and escalate security alerts to appropriate personnel; (d) establish, document, and distribute security incident response and escalation procedures to ensure timely and effective handling of incidents; (e) administer user accounts, including additions, deletions, and modifications; and (f) monitor and control all access to data. These responsibilities must be centrally managed to ensure consistent implementation, compliance, and continuous monitoring across the organization. 

<!-- evidence:48500c180c77571c1871d24f source:Legal Clause Definitions!C4 -->
"Security Officer" means an individual designated by the Vendor with overall responsibility and authority to manage the organization’s Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program, including implementing policies, monitoring compliance, and overseeing incident response and access control.

"Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (“CDPP”)" means a comprehensive, documented program that consolidates an organization’s cybersecurity and data protection policies, standards, and procedures into a single policy. 

<!-- evidence:85ca0ee30e4a88a99a967c0e source:Legal Clause Definitions!D4 -->
Regodit requires that all vendors ensure clear accountability and centralized management of cybersecurity responsibilities. By mandating executive support and assigning authority to a designated security officer, the provision guarantees that critical functions are formally documented, consistently implemented, and effectively enforced. This structure reduces risk, supports regulatory compliance, and prevents fragmented security practices that could expose Regodit to operational, legal, and reputational vulnerabilities.

<!-- evidence:9e7ae9a699d81f75936e2556 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E4 -->

<!-- evidence:37ae9cfbb42548a8ad11cb2f source:Legal Clause Definitions!A5 -->
Cybersecurity Oversight and Continuous Monitoring

<!-- evidence:ffb751897a5c1dc60bbc4ecd source:Legal Clause Definitions!B5 -->
 Vendor shall implement and maintain a robust CDPP control framework that meets all applicable statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements. Vendor's designated Security Officer, or its representative(s), shall: (a) continuously improve detection and protection capabilities; (b) employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor cybersecurity and data protection controls on an ongoing basis; (c) review the control framework at least annually to reflect changes impacting business processes; (d) perform quarterly reviews of security operations to identify and remediate nonconformities, including daily log reviews, firewall ruleset reviews, application of configuration standards to new systems, response to security alerts, and change management processes; (e) maintain documentation of all reviews, including results and sign-off by authorized personnel; and (f) present oversight results to the organization’s risk and/or audit committees.

<!-- evidence:605a0af7408f194a13acf37b source:Legal Clause Definitions!C5 -->
"Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program (“CDPP”)" means a comprehensive, documented program that consolidates an organization’s cybersecurity and data protection policies, standards, and procedures into a single policy.

"Security Officer" means an individual designated by the Vendor with overall responsibility and authority to manage the organization’s Cybersecurity and Data Protection Program, including implementing policies, monitoring compliance, and overseeing incident response and access control.

<!-- evidence:357b6a0f9fe94b6e919ff2f0 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D5 -->
Regodit requires all vendors to ensure a structured, continuous, and independent approach to cybersecurity oversight. By mandating a robust control framework, regular reviews, and documented processes, it guarantees that detection, protection, and compliance measures remain current and effective. Independent assessments and quarterly operational reviews reduce risk, prevent policy nonconformities, and support regulatory and contractual obligations. These requirements provide transparency, accountability, and audit readiness, safeguarding Regodit’s technology assets and sensitive data against evolving threats.

<!-- evidence:1377beec205fcfe699766264 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E5 -->

<!-- evidence:2caec8e88475607989928011 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A6 -->
Supply Chain Cybersecurity Safeguards

<!-- evidence:86ec03f727171da6e6f28839 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B6 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain documented procurement safeguards to mitigate cybersecurity and data privacy risks within the supply chain and reduce exposure to legal and financial liabilities. At a minimum, Vendor shall: (a) avoid procurement of custom configurations that increase supply chain risk; (b) utilize a diverse set of suppliers to reduce dependency on any single source; (c) source only from vendors with established industry reputations; and (d) apply procurement carve-outs or exclusions where necessary to protect Regodit’s technology assets and Regodit Data. Vendor shall require its subcontractors to implement and follow procedures at least as stringent as these. 

<!-- evidence:6faa3ddf49a56514f5edff79 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C6 -->
 

<!-- evidence:f7706fdc5b77eaadcd530505 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D6 -->
Regodit requires all Vendors to mitigate supply chain cybersecurity risks that could expose Regodit to operational, legal, and financial liabilities. These measures reduce the likelihood of advanced persistent threats targeting the supply chain and help maintain compliance with obligations, protecting Regodit’s technology assets and sensitive data.

<!-- evidence:d17718637dfaee64b0993c4c source:Legal Clause Definitions!A7 -->
Cybersecurity and Data Protection Workforce Development

<!-- evidence:b85715043b9ba0eae7edeca4 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B7 -->
Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain a Cybersecurity and Data Protection Workforce Development Program. At a minimum, the program shall: (a) provide initial and ongoing cybersecurity and data protection literacy training for all employees, contractors, and third-party users, including orientation for new users and annual refresher training; (b) ensure individuals with access to Regodit Data are informed of relevant policy, standard, and procedure updates; and (c) maintain documentation of all training activities and updates.

<!-- evidence:30e3a3af6744d39c42e1270a source:Legal Clause Definitions!C7 -->
"Cybersecurity and Data Protection Workforce Development Program" means a structured program designed to ensure that all personnel, including employees, contractors, and third-party users, receive initial and ongoing training on cybersecurity and data protection practices.

<!-- evidence:11cbee05ff6588b3209cc6cc source:Legal Clause Definitions!D7 -->
Regodit requires all vendors to ensure a structured, role‑based, and continuously improving workforce capability around cybersecurity and data protection.

<!-- evidence:4a8591588abfddd5d65ad19b source:Legal Clause Definitions!A8 -->
Cybersecurity and Data Protection Training

<!-- evidence:319544e54d7ed6c278ce89c1 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B8 -->
 Vendor shall develop, implement, and run, at least once annually, a formal Cybersecurity and Data Protection Literacy Training Program for all Vendor personnel with access to Regodit systems or Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:509e3f6c9e3c7131efe1040c source:Legal Clause Definitions!C8 -->
"Cybersecurity and Data Protection Literacy Training Program" means a program that provides initial and ongoing training to personnel and third-party users on cybersecurity and data protection practices specific to their roles to ensure awareness, compliance, and risk mitigation.

<!-- evidence:1590b6382b9c1ef0400c0bcf source:Legal Clause Definitions!D8 -->
Regodit requires all vendors maintain robust cybersecurity and data protection practices by requiring formal training for all personnel with access to Regodit systems or data.This mitigates risks associated with human error, strengthens compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and promotes consistent awareness of evolving threats and security protocols.

Data Privacy Program

<!-- evidence:e7c8ab77fe38b2dc1e378219 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B9 -->
Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain an up-to-date, comprehensive Data Privacy Program and operational processes to ensure adherence to applicable privacy protection laws, regulations, and contractual obligations. Vendor agrees to incorporate appropriate safeguards, policies, and procedures to ensure the proper handling of Personal Data and to promptly update such measures as necessary to address regulatory changes or identified risks.

<!-- evidence:dfd0caa18c15b6ba4cead24b source:Legal Clause Definitions!C9 -->
 "Data Privacy Program" means a documented framework of policies, standards, and procedures designed to ensure the secure collection, use, retention, and disposal of personal data in compliance with applicable statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements

<!-- evidence:ca91e4dcb881d9ec570024a7 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D9 -->
Regodit requires all vendors to  establish and maintain a comprehensive data privacy program in adhereance with applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations.

<!-- evidence:42eded4a35a5ad4849db1278 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A13 -->
Encryption of Sensitive Data

<!-- evidence:b08b831ddaee050745424091 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B13 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain processes and technical measures to protect Sensitive Regodit Data in transit and at rest through the use of strong Encryption Protocols, in compliance with applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory requirements. Vendor shall ensure that sensitive data is never stored in cleartext, employ industry-standard encryption algorithms (e.g., AES-256) in validated formats, and verify proper encryption strength and secure configurations. Vendor shall review all relevant data sources, including logs, transaction data, and memory files, to confirm that Sensitive Regodit Data is not retained in human-readable format.

<!-- evidence:5cbbb1b109ecf28c8cb84368 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C13 -->
"Encryption Protocols" means standardized methods and algorithms used to secure data by converting it into an unreadable format during storage, processing, or transmission, ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and compliance with applicable security requirements.

<!-- evidence:79ef7fd1481e5560001c0b0f source:Legal Clause Definitions!D13 -->

<!-- evidence:578a4d05f9b7515f6a0bfb97 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A16 -->
Data Protection and Retention

<!-- evidence:5cfafe3bfc076fd47d108c47 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B16 -->
Vendor shall implement controls to protect Regodit Data wherever it is stored, transmitted, or processed, in compliance with all applicable statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations. Vendor shall define and adhere to retention periods for both Sensitive Data and Non-Sensitive Data and establish processes to securely dispose of, destroy, erase, or anonymize data once it is no longer required for business purposes. 

<!-- evidence:a72fa871f93c2a9c4007eb90 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C16 -->
"Sensitive Data" means information that requires protection due to its confidential nature or regulatory classification, including but not limited to Personally Identifiable Information ("PII"), financial data, health records, intellectual property, and any data whose unauthorized disclosure, alteration, or destruction could result in harm or legal liability.                                                                                                                 

"Non-Sensitive Data" means information that does not require special protection under statutory, regulatory, or contractual obligations and whose unauthorized disclosure, alteration, or destruction would not result in harm, legal liability, or compromise confidentiality.                                                                                        

<!-- evidence:6a8877fa8f9bfff9af550fa3 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D16 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors maintain strict controls over the protection, retention, and disposal of Regodit Data in compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.

<!-- evidence:253daa5c54621022b67f9d19 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A18 -->
Physical Access Control

<!-- evidence:5f127fdf925c540cecdcfc8c source:Legal Clause Definitions!B18 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain processes to control physical access to facilities and areas where Regodit Data or systems are stored, processed, or accessed. Vendor shall maintain an access list of authorized personnel, restrict access based on assigned roles and responsibilities, issue and manage physical access credentials, and review and update access lists at least every ninety (90) days. Vendor shall immediately revoke access and disable all physical access mechanisms (e.g., keys, access cards) upon termination or when access is no longer required. Access to areas containing sensitive or regulated data shall be granted only to personnel with a legitimate business need.

<!-- evidence:f428a4d2fbf536147f9531b1 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D18 -->

<!-- evidence:d31e39413320d0045268f67c source:Legal Clause Definitions!A20 -->
Asset Management

<!-- evidence:0d6775a15f44623eff96fac5 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B20 -->
Vendor shall establish and maintain an IT Asset Management  Program ("ITAMP") that inventories all technology assets used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data. The ITAMP shall include hardware and software inventories for both internally and externally hosted assets; a method to accurately identify asset owner, contact information, and purpose; a list of Regodit-approved technology assets; and, where technically feasible, a list of all personnel with access to these assets. Vendor shall review and update inventory records at least quarterly to ensure accuracy and accountability.

<!-- evidence:f8118b555c97c555d1f37920 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C20 -->
 "IT Asset Management  Program ("ITAMP")" means a structured program that inventories, tracks, and manages all hardware, software, and related technology assets within an organization to ensure accountability, security, compliance, and proper lifecycle management.

<!-- evidence:713656ba3e96b3f2cee7a45b source:Legal Clause Definitions!D20 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors maintain accurate and up-to-date inventories of all technology assets used to store, process, or transmit Regodit data. Without proper IT asset management, organizations face risks such as unauthorized access, unpatched systems, duplicate accounting, and loss of accountability for hardware and software components.

<!-- evidence:30bb91e833f57e06b359fd9c source:Legal Clause Definitions!A21 -->
Data Transmission Security

<!-- evidence:c4b638e2df49756983e10962 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B21 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain processes and technical measures to prevent unauthorized disclosure of Regodit Data during transmission over internal, external, public, or private networks. Vendor shall ensure that only trusted keys and certificates are accepted, use strong cryptography and secure protocols (e.g., TLS, IPsec, SSH) to safeguard sensitive or regulated data, and verify encryption strength based on industry-recognized practices. Vendor shall configure protocols securely, prohibit insecure versions, and ensure HTTPS is used for all web-based transmissions involving Sensitive Regodit Data.

<!-- evidence:a0a481d65ab3ab286f40e46b source:Legal Clause Definitions!C21 -->
 

<!-- evidence:308b01e5134c4607b02b8118 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D21 -->

<!-- evidence:8b01715a67459554b047c6b3 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A23 -->
System Documentation and Secure Configuration

<!-- evidence:5944c60cbae79ce1153b12ff source:Legal Clause Definitions!B23 -->
Vendor maintains and shall continue to maintain documented secure development policies, procedures, and standards consistent with industry-recognized security practices for the development and maintenance of its software concerning administrator and user features, functions, and vulnerabilities. Vendor shall ensure developers provide detailed documentation of security and privacy controls, external system interfaces, architectural design, and source code for custom-developed applications to enable analysis and testing. 

<!-- evidence:8edea21e5a7c6094e3b82605 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C23 -->
 

<!-- evidence:af39765cb98198f8508eccb3 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D23 -->

Clear administrator and user guidance, and detailed developer documentation enable effective security management, incident response, and auditability.

<!-- evidence:42f445b9ce607a30ba7b0706 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A24 -->
Secure Software Development Requirments

<!-- evidence:cc5df5455f9bd053189d4b5c source:Legal Clause Definitions!B24 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain a documented software development process that explicitly addresses cybersecurity and data privacy requirements throughout the Software Development Life Cycle ("SDLC"). Vendor shall adopt industry-recognized secure coding practices applicable to the programming languages used, ensure developers receive annual training on secure coding techniques, and prevent inclusion of development artifacts in production environments. Vendor shall ensure all custom code is reviewed prior to release by qualified personnel other than the original author, with corrections implemented and management approval obtained before deployment. Vendor shall incorporate controls to mitigate common vulnerabilities and attacks, including injection flaws, cryptographic weaknesses, access control exploits, and business logic abuses.

<!-- evidence:240f407cef9483a5f4ecdbdf source:Legal Clause Definitions!C24 -->
 "Software Development Life Cycle ("SDLC")" means a structured process for planning, designing, developing, testing, deploying, and maintaining software applications, incorporating secure coding practices and controls throughout each phase to ensure functionality, security, and compliance.

<!-- evidence:fb42a67083e8c86ab80f06da source:Legal Clause Definitions!D24 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors follow secure software development practices that integrate cybersecurity and data privacy throughout the Software Development Life Cycle. Without these measures, applications may contain vulnerabilities that can be exploited, leading to data breaches, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational harm that Regodit cannot accept.

<!-- evidence:1b549c45ccd32612de9c2a42 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A25 -->
Vulnerability Management 

<!-- evidence:04a99048774913e63589da48 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B25 -->
Vendor shall perform vulnerability scans at least once annually on all systems and hosted applications used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data, utilizing authenticated scanning tools and techniques that identify software flaws, improper configurations, and measure vulnerability impact. Vendor shall analyze scan results, track findings through a documented remediation plan, and remediate vulnerabilities based on a risk-based timeline: high-risk within thirty (30) days, moderate-risk within ninety (90) days, and low-risk within one hundred eighty (180) days of discovery. 

<!-- evidence:deabc3b7b138fb75611601d1 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C25 -->
 

<!-- evidence:ef6b5de94ca071358a8d64d8 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D25 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors proactively self-audit their security systems to identify and remediate vulnerabilities in systems and applications that handle Regodit Data.

<!-- evidence:be3320307f3f1c41ad3a140b source:Legal Clause Definitions!A27 -->
Security Incident Event Management

<!-- evidence:c5ddf5f1f9f577491f50a6e3 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B27 -->
Vendor shall configure all systems, applications, and services used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data to implement automated audit trails for all system components and forward security-related event logs to a centralized log collector, Security Incident Event Management System ("SIEMS"), or equivalent solution. Vendor shall ensure logs capture key events, including account logon attempts, account management changes, object access, policy changes, privilege use, process tracking, and system events, as well as administrator activity and data actions for web-based applications. Vendor shall monitor for anomalous behaviors, generate weekly reports of unusual activity, report findings to Regodit cybersecurity personnel as required by Regodit, and adjust audit review levels based on changes in risk or credible threat intelligence.

<!-- evidence:bab981fa1e5d556fe32e42b6 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C27 -->
"Security Incident Event Management System ("SIEMS")" means a technology solution that aggregates, monitors, and analyzes security-related event logs from multiple systems to detect, investigate, and respond to potential cybersecurity incidents in real time.

<!-- evidence:6b042629e8710d3fa3569ca5 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D27 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors implement robust audit logging and centralized event monitoring to detect and respond to security incidents effectively where Regodit Data could be at risk.

Network Security Controls

<!-- evidence:248399379477ab85f75360ea source:Legal Clause Definitions!B28 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain cybersecurity and data privacy controls to protect all communications and wireless networks used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data. Vendor shall ensure that security controls for network services are identified, documented, and incorporated into technical requirements and any network service agreements, whether services are provided internally or through third-party providers.

<!-- evidence:5fc8a2637d6ce33d4893dcc7 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C28 -->
 

<!-- evidence:3bf51129890242aceb562fe1 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D28 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors secure communications and data transmitted across wireless networks. 

<!-- evidence:c2d33d37807313b0d00e673b source:Legal Clause Definitions!E28 -->
NET-01

<!-- evidence:f2f5e197cdcf1be142816588 source:Legal Clause Definitions!F28 -->

<!-- evidence:aea02399b94b1640a660ae50 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A29 -->
Incident Response and Management

<!-- evidence:d937146b0b8d70dd8405e1f4 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B29 -->
Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain an Incident Response Plan ("IRP") to ensure timely and effective management of cybersecurity-related events impacting Regodit Data or systems. The IRP shall include processes for immediate response to incidents, annual testing, designation of 24/7 on-call personnel, and staff training for breach response responsibilities. Vendor shall notify Regodit within forty-eight (48) hours of discovering a Security Incident has occured with all information Regodit may deem necessary to comply with applicable data privacy laws. 

<!-- evidence:ec005b7f52bbb94785920306 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C29 -->
 "Incident Response Plan ("IRP")" means a documented set of procedures outlining how an organization detects, responds to, and recovers from cybersecurity incidents, including roles, responsibilities, communication protocols, and steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate threats.

<!-- evidence:e19d60f40fac993f29441ed8 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D29 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors have a robust and tested incident response capability to quickly detect, contain, and remediate cybersecurity incidents. Regodit further requires Vendor notify Regodit of all incidents so Regodit is able to comply with all requirements placed on Regodit by applicable data privacy laws. 

<!-- evidence:e1d99a03800192eec2cb575f source:Legal Clause Definitions!E29 -->
IRO-04

<!-- evidence:499dc3a4948d5f149db6a805 source:Legal Clause Definitions!F29 -->

<!-- evidence:00968ba0c26cbcb3e4ec322c source:Legal Clause Definitions!A30 -->
Cybersecurity Event Response and Management

<!-- evidence:3800e0a94539e8a360c72a20 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B30 -->
Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain processes and technical measures to ensure timely and effective management of cybersecurity-related events impacting Regodit Data or systems (an "Incident Response Plan"). Vendor shall perform periodic testing to confirm the capabilities of the Incident ResponsePplan are effective at least once annually. 

<!-- evidence:9ac074faaa10c09952a43be4 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C30 -->
 

<!-- evidence:dd1e69b2051ec0b4756240be source:Legal Clause Definitions!D30 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors can rapidly detect, triage, and remediate cybersecurity incidents impacting Regodit’s data or systems. A formal, tested Incident Response Plan is integral to the security of Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:e065b4411794914304915b1e source:Legal Clause Definitions!E30 -->
IRO-04

<!-- evidence:76639ccdf5f4855ad214345f source:Legal Clause Definitions!A31 -->
Security Event Notification

<!-- evidence:399a2e4d67b50efdbe420f3e source:Legal Clause Definitions!B31 -->
 Vendor shall implement controls to ensure the secure notification to Regodit in the event that any information security event, including a Data Breach or suspected security incident, occurs and affects Regodit Data.  Vendor shall notify Regodit within forty-eight (48) hours of such information security event. 

<!-- evidence:290ed8c1b2bf7ec38c5851d6 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C31 -->
“Data Breach” means a breach of Vendor’s security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, or unauthorized disclosure of, or access to Regodit Data. Data Breach shall not include unsuccessful attempts or activities that do not compromise the security of Regodit Data, including unsuccessful log-in attempts, pings, port scans, denial of service attacks, and other network attacks on firewalls or networked systems.                                                                                                          

<!-- evidence:ba5f92f5e2a8b6ddc71f1a10 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D31 -->
Regodit mandates all Vendors have a system in place to notify Regodit if any security event takes place involving Regodit Data.

<!-- evidence:9015a0823e4753449a46c277 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A33 -->
Workplace Security Controls

<!-- evidence:80edffccee9606bc808cb9db source:Legal Clause Definitions!B33 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain industry standard anti-virus and endpoint protection software to protect workstations and peripheral assets used to access or process Regodit Data. These measures shall include: (a) disabling user computing sessions after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity; (b) proper disposal of physical media in accordance with document destruction policies; (c) clearing work areas of all media containing sensitive or regulated data when unattended; (d) locking filing cabinets, drawers, storage rooms, and other units containing sensitive data when not in use; and (e) sanitizing shared work surfaces such as whiteboards, cork boards, and writing tablets when not in use.

<!-- evidence:3f43ffd7088d6470a078e132 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C33 -->
 

<!-- evidence:9d797527876d6802a0841c40 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D33 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors maintain strong physical and workplace security practices to protect sensitive and regulated data.

<!-- evidence:a892bb066dd8f16af3253fa5 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A34 -->
IT Asset Management

<!-- evidence:7e073bca8245009a29fd57e6 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B34 -->
 Vendor respresents that it (a) maintains accurate inventories of hardware and software assets, including internally and externally hosted components; (b) maintains a method to identify asset owner, contact information, and purpose; (c) reviews and updates inventories at least quarterly; and (d) where technically feasible, maintains a list of all personnel with access to these assets.

<!-- evidence:7f261204c66488f2f2230e59 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C34 -->
 

<!-- evidence:97ecf71caced2b84ee56d15a source:Legal Clause Definitions!D34 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors maintain accurate and up-to-date inventories of all technology assets used to store, process, or transmit Regodit data.

<!-- evidence:14c442fb18ca6a543f8e4b0c source:Legal Clause Definitions!A35 -->
Identity and Access Management Controls

<!-- evidence:935a1d92f9564bf7940cefb8 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B35 -->
Vendor shall implement and maintain industry-recognized and regulatory-compliant organization-wide policies, processes, and technical measures that govern user identification, authentication, authorization, and account lifecycle management to ensure secure and appropriate access for all systems used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:aaf46f53eb8c127f2f79dca6 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C35 -->
 

<!-- evidence:c15ac170bd163d02681f6ef4 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D35 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors implement strong identity and access management controls to protect systems handling Regodit data and Regodit Data itself from unauthorized access.

<!-- evidence:cfd30b4eb1da01e826b060f6 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E35 -->
IAC-01

<!-- evidence:cd92b44461909605c1e9b158 source:Legal Clause Definitions!F35 -->

<!-- evidence:60b9b6fe285b5d45846c12ba source:Legal Clause Definitions!A36 -->
Role-Based Access Control

<!-- evidence:4b9a9b89104c7992b14d973a source:Legal Clause Definitions!B36 -->
Vendor shall restrict system and data access based on a user’s assigned role, granting only the minimum permissions necessary to perform authorized job functions in accordance with the principle of least privilege for all systems, applications, and services used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:39d20e94b5fa0dc8f66e5913 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C36 -->
 

<!-- evidence:de2e410c765333450340f3aa source:Legal Clause Definitions!D36 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors enforce the principle of least privilege through Role-Based Access Control . Without Role-Based Access Control, users or system accounts may have excessive permissions, increasing the risk of unauthorized access, privilege escalation, and data breaches. 

<!-- evidence:8c593955a81cd474d7f1e3e0 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E36 -->
IAC-08

<!-- evidence:b81f799d990947d19ebb7ffd source:Legal Clause Definitions!F36 -->

<!-- evidence:f9003cb0c6ff14caa3d0faff source:Legal Clause Definitions!A37 -->
External Authenticator Compliance

<!-- evidence:4567bdc809075e6e6718e696 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B37 -->
Vendor shall restrict the use of external authenticators to those that are fully compliant with National Institute of Standards and Technology ("NIST") requirements, including NIST SP 800-63B guidelines. Vendor shall maintain and provide, upon request, a list of accepted external authenticators that meet or exceed applicable technical, security, privacy, and organizational standards.

<!-- evidence:023c1c83499615a8de9f63b8 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C37 -->
 

<!-- evidence:fd9a7b960a9b1608a627be18 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D37 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors use only NIST-compliant external authenticators for systems and services, particularly those accessible to the public.

<!-- evidence:0b690e84016ab6c04e8fa573 source:Legal Clause Definitions!E37 -->
IAC-03.5

<!-- evidence:9f5790f979fa46ba44ea3123 source:Legal Clause Definitions!F37 -->
Formula: =TRIM(CLEAN(SUBSTITUTE(E37,CHAR(160),""))); source cached value: 'IAC-03.5' (not independently recalculated)

<!-- evidence:32f4a107c6a9e39864db58f8 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A38 -->
Principle of Least Privilege

<!-- evidence:19b9b5c2712f9031599b7de9 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B38 -->
Vendor shall only grant the minimum permissions necessary to each user for such user to perform their authorized job functions in accordance with the principle of least privilege for all systems, applications, and services used to store, process, or transmit Regodit Data.  Vendor shall ensure that system processes operate at privilege levels no higher than necessary and apply least privilege principles to account creation, system design, development, and operations.

<!-- evidence:2b49be0d6a084f4ebb18aaa2 source:Legal Clause Definitions!C38 -->
 

<!-- evidence:7520c959a667f764bfde85b3 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D38 -->
Regodit requires this provision to ensure vendors enforce the principle of least privilege, granting only the minimum access necessary for job functions and for the shortest time required. Without these controls, excessive permissions increase the risk of unauthorized access, privilege escalation, and data breaches.

<!-- evidence:a29f35057201fc2cad72f763 source:Legal Clause Definitions!F38 -->

<!-- evidence:016cdc81cb636920436cf29a source:Legal Clause Definitions!A39 -->
Cybersecurity Risk Management Program

<!-- evidence:57729435cd69e74f14b08572 source:Legal Clause Definitions!B39 -->
Vendor shall conduct a security risk assessment at least once annually which identifies, assesses, and mitigates cybersecurity risks to organizational systems and data, incorporating industry-recognized methodologies, periodic risk assessments, and continuous monitoring to ensure compliance and resilience.

<!-- evidence:9ea42a5685efaa8debbcf59d source:Legal Clause Definitions!C39 -->
 

<!-- evidence:405d130c44f75eddf5688c04 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D39 -->

<!-- evidence:c928bfd5ace3f462845b3a76 source:Legal Clause Definitions!A40 -->
Penetrations Testing and Vulnerability Assessments

<!-- evidence:604923455075ad5a632e1e2b source:Legal Clause Definitions!B40 -->
Vendor conducts regularly scheduled penetration testing. Further, Vendor will complete internal and external vulnerability scans of its systems and Services periodically, and will update and patch operating systems, applications, firewalls, and all other in-scope systems and applications and remediate or mitigate all such vulnerabilities in accordance with industry standard timelines based on risk.

<!-- evidence:6a93c7881915e868b955c51d source:Legal Clause Definitions!C40 -->
 

<!-- evidence:459267b584b56f6c5719cc56 source:Legal Clause Definitions!D40 -->

<!-- evidence:0671aa5604fd3f150a3cc24f source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A3 -->
Vendor Liability for Regodit Data

<!-- evidence:267cefc5f6dcb997042f8eed source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B3 -->
Vendor acknowledges and understands that Vendor is wholly responsible and liable for the security of Regodit Data that the Vendor has in its possession or that it otherwise processes, stores, or transmits. Vendor shall notify Regodit of any actual or suspected security incident or Data Breach affecting Regodit Data within 24 hours of discovery and provide regular updates until resolution.

<!-- evidence:b54b6d4186c0cc471c2ae433 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!C3 -->
“Data Breach” means a breach of Vendor’s security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, or unauthorized disclosure of, or access to Regodit Data. Data Breach shall not include unsuccessful attempts or activities that do not compromise the security of Regodit Data, including unsuccessful log-in attempts, pings, port scans, denial of service attacks, and other network attacks on firewalls or networked systems.

<!-- evidence:fd27a0581e1204a5f273d3d6 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D3 -->
Regodit mandates all Vendors accept liability for the secure handling and storage of Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:14b1deb7e9b4f6ca7971da3a source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!E3 -->

<!-- evidence:8256620b2f40f4ca8d67db89 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A4 -->
Confidentiality of and Access to Regodit Data

<!-- evidence:24b0aa2776a03292d2878b88 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B4 -->
Vendor shall hold in the strictest confidence all data which it receives, creates, stores, or otherwise processes for, on behalf of, or in Vendor's provision of the Services to Regodit, including, but not limited to, Regodit Personal Data (collectively, "Regodit Data"). Vendor shall ensure that all persons authorized to access Regodit Data are made aware of the confidential nature of such data, have received appropriate training on their responsibilities, and have committed themselves to confidentiality (e.g., by confidentiality agreements) or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality. Vendor Shall ensure that Vendor's access to Regodit Data is limited to those personnel performing Services in accordance with the Agreement. Regodit Data shall only be accessed and processed for the performance of the Services set forth herein. 

<!-- evidence:71568d4383580309effb7347 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!C4 -->
“Regodit Personal Data” means any Personal Data that Vendor receives, creates, stores, or otherwise processes for, on behalf of, or in Vendor's provision of the Services to Regodit. 

“Personal Data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable living individual, including information that can be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular data subject and is protected as “personal data”, “personal information”, or “personally identifiable information”, under applicable data protection laws.

“Data Subject” means an identified or identifiable natural person whom Personal Data relates.

<!-- evidence:58b4356f69b6c95881c005cf source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D4 -->
Regodit requires Vendor to maintain the confidentiality of Regodit Data and hold their personnel to the same standard, implementing the standard that only those who need access to perform the services will have access. 

<!-- evidence:8aa18da94b741fc4f49d2721 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!E4 -->
TPM-5

<!-- evidence:e1aae25262c9ac0966e302b8 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D5 -->

<!-- evidence:41fcd0c4a0bbfc18bf783f96 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A7 -->
Vendor Liability for Data Breach Costs

<!-- evidence:dbecfae395ebec745caf874b source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B7 -->
To the extent that a Data Breach gives rise to a need for Regodit, in its sole discretion, to: (a) provide notification to government authorities, individuals, Data Subjects, or other persons; or (b) further investigate the Data Breach and to undertake certain remedial measures, as well as certain other mitigtion, remedial or corrective actions in respect of the Data Breach, including, without limitation, root cause analysis, credit monitoring or identity protection services, or call center services (collectively, “Remedial Action”), and Vendor shall promptly reimburse Regodit for the foregoing, as well as all legal, accounting, IT, and other costs and expenses incurred by Regodit related to the Data Breach. The timing, content, and manner of providing any notices to Data Subjects shall be determined by Regodit. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section shall not be subject to the limitations of liability set forth herein.

<!-- evidence:af14940ec65be8941771ab86 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D7 -->
Vendor must be responsible for paying the costs and expenses associated with the remedial measures that must be taken following a data breach caused by Vendor.

<!-- evidence:0c42df392dae591ce83ab71e source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A8 -->
Regodit Data Deletion

<!-- evidence:5585050bd9e5ee5bc4224e41 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B8 -->
Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement (in whole or in part), or earlier upon Regodit's request, Vendor shall destroy all Regodit Data processed, accessed, or stored by Vendor, and any copies thereof, and certify, upon Regodit's request, that Vendor has done so, unless any applicable law, competent court, supervisory authority, or regulatory body prevents Vendor from destroying Regodit Data whereby, if so, all security requirements and obligations of Vendor set forth herein shall remain in effect and applicable to Vendor until the Vendor has destroyed all Regodit Data. 

<!-- evidence:1c68e996b1568af504bcc5ab source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D8 -->
Regodit requests that Vendor delete all Regodit Data upon the expiration or termination of the agreement.

<!-- evidence:4a22610d029c518b9c330b0b source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A9 -->
Termination for Breach of Security

<!-- evidence:996151020144fe2bcf7898e5 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B9 -->
Regodit may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Vendor, and without fault, penalty, or liability, if Vendor is found by Regodit, in its sole discretion,  to be violating the security requirements or data protection obligations  imposed on Vendor by this Agreement. Such violation shall be considered a material breach of this Agreement. 

<!-- evidence:722ee69be64806ec83ed3a62 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D9 -->
If Vendor is found to be violating the security requirements imposed under this agreement, Regodit must have the right to terminate the agreement and cease the relationship, as Regodit must protect its client's personal data. 

<!-- evidence:3f2e0bfeaa957e1c33f6bb97 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!E9 -->

<!-- evidence:5f3d535ef1a1493207aa34b6 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A10 -->
Audit of Security Complaince

<!-- evidence:e40fecf4320ef9472c96d4ec source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B10 -->
At the Regodit's written request, Vendor will, once annually or if following a Data Breach, allow an audit to verify Vendor's compliance with security obligations imposed by this Agreement and under applicable data protection laws. If a defect is found in Vendor's compliance with the security measures set forth in [schedule/exhibit X] herein, Vendor shall cure the defect immediately and supply Regodit with a written statement indicating remediation upon cure. 

<!-- evidence:a287fd4f9bca515cf2a3aaff source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D10 -->
Regodit must maintain the right to audit Vendor's security compliance for as long as Vendor processes or stores Regodit Data. If a defect is found, Vendor must immediately remedy it and provide Regodit of notice of such remedition when completed.

<!-- evidence:f182a57a89a841fe845425f9 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A13 -->
Subcontractor Contractual Requirements

<!-- evidence:5c812c3f45df09006031ab33 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B13 -->
Vendor represents and warrants that Vendor maintains written agreements with all subcontractos which obligate such subcontractors to comply  with cybersecurity and data protection and privacy measures, as well as confidentiality obligations, at least as stringent as Regodit's requirements set forth in this Agreement, and which obligate such subcontractors to contact Regodit, without delay, for any request to vary the compliance requirements. Vendor shall ensure Regodit has the right to audit subcontractors’ compliance with security requirements upon reasonable notice.

<!-- evidence:7b6ad2424e568f62e5c84355 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D13 -->
Regodit mandates all service providers to bind their subcontractors in written agreements to comply with security and privacy measures at least as stringent as Regodit's, which requirements can be found at/in: [insert url or refence to schedule/exhibit within the document].

<!-- evidence:25f4cf2f695727360d2e6bb6 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A14 -->
Unique Authentication for Customer Accounts

<!-- evidence:b4ae75488c9bf5fcf30469d3 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B14 -->
Vendor shall employ unique authentication factors and protocols to each Regodit Customer account. At least once annually, and upon Regodit's written request, Vendor shall provide Regodit with a first-party declaration confirming Vendor complies with such obligation. Vendor shall enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all administrative and privileged access to systems processing Regodit Data.

<!-- evidence:d0244c5c488ce783abc888dd source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D14 -->
Regodit prioritizes its customers' security and must be able to confirm the same.

<!-- evidence:42a360fb5e26a4c05cacfa62 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A16 -->
CRM

<!-- evidence:b674e34ecf61b362d4e58c9d source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B16 -->
Vendor shall maintain, comply with, and provide to Regodit a Customer Responsibility Matrix (a "CRM"), in such form which is acceptable to Regodit in its sole discretion, or, if Vendor does not have a CRM in effect or if Regodit deems such Vendor-provided CRM to not be acceptable, Vendor shall then comply with, and therefore agrees to comply with,  the CRM provided be Regodit in [exhibit/schedule X].

<!-- evidence:fa1ae10a2381b80ce6be2bf5 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D16 -->
Regodit maintains a responsible, accountable, support, consulted, and inform service matrix with all Vendors to delineate assignment for cybersecurity & data privacy controls between internal stakeholders and External Service Providers. As such, Regodit requests a CRM be in place for the term of this engagement with Vendor.

<!-- evidence:260ba165aa793af97425a156 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A17 -->
Security Changes

<!-- evidence:0aaa296507f6189408e71434 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B17 -->
Vendor must notify Regodit in writing it Vendor intends to modify its  security or data protection processes or policies or the Services such that new security or data protection measures are to be/must be established. Such changes must be approved by Regodit prior to the Vendor's implementation. If such changes are not approved by Regodit, Vendor must maintain the secuirty and data protection processes and policies as were in place as of the date of this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain a secure software development lifecycle (SDLC), including code reviews, vulnerability scanning, and timely patching of identified risks.

<!-- evidence:86b1dd6a1cd23515ea5b042d source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D17 -->
Regodit must be notified if there is an expected change in security or data protection processes or policies and must have an approval right, as such measures are of high importance in the contemplation of this Agreement in order to secure Regodit's customers' data.

<!-- evidence:a27e49b86c8d67d5fcae015b source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!A18 -->
Data Storage

<!-- evidence:a60072d16e3d914db5b127e0 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!B18 -->
Vendor will process and store all data within the United States of America. If any data is processed or stored outside such territory, Vendor shall promptly notify Regodit of the location and purpose of such processessing and storage. Vendor shall ensure any cross-border data transfers comply with applicable data protection laws and shall implement appropriate safeguards.

<!-- evidence:18dd6753ce467583674ca085 source:Legal Clause Definitions-TPRM!D18 -->
Regodit needs to be aware of where Regodit data is being processed and stored in order to comply with applicable data protection laws.
